correctness.rationale: The Cayley--Dickson product splits the map at a fixed quaternion argument into two matrix-linear blocks. Rank-one pair orthogonality is exactly the common-image/common-kernel dichotomy. In the first case the displayed 2-by-4 matrix has rank two and the other block has determinant 2t(ad-bc), hence rank four; in the second case the 4-by-4 determinant is -(ad-bc)^2 and the other block is right multiplication by a rank-one matrix, hence rank two. This exhausts the hypotheses for all fields of characteristic not two. Exhaustive normalized finite-field tests over GF(3), GF(5) and GF(7) replay successfully; they are not needed for infinite-field proof.
